title: Qvidian vs Responsive (2026): A Buyer's Comparison of Two Enterprise RFP Platforms
summary: Compare Qvidian and Responsive on pricing, AI answering, integrations, and reviews plus a look at the AI-native alternative reshaping RFP response.
body_markdown:
**Last reviewed:** January 2026. This comparison draws on vendor-published materials, verified reviews across G2, Capterra, and TrustRadius, and independent third-party analyses. Both vendors price by quote and ship feature updates frequently, so read every figure here as a point-in-time snapshot — verify current pricing, editions, and capabilities with each vendor before you commit.


## **TL;DR: Qvidian vs Responsive**


Qvidian fits teams that want a mature, content-library-centric proposal engine with deep Microsoft Office integration — common in large financial services, technology, and healthcare organizations. Responsive fits teams that want a broad answer library plus AI-driven answering across RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires, with strong project collaboration. Which is better? It depends on what your team needs: Qvidian leans toward document assembly and library governance; Responsive leans toward AI answering, breadth of integrations, and multi-format response management. If you're shortlisting at the enterprise level, it's also worth scanning how a newer wave of AI-native enterprise RFP platforms tackles the same job with a different architecture.


## **What Should You Consider When Choosing Between Qvidian and Responsive?**


Before the feature tables, map these criteria to how your team actually responds to RFPs. Answer each question during your demos.


• **AI capabilities:** Does the tool draft answers, or just retrieve stored ones? How much editing do drafts need?


• **Response quality:** Test edge-case questions. How often are top-ranked answers actually usable as-is?


• **Content management and governance:** How do you keep the library current, and who owns that maintenance?


• **Conflict and duplicate detection:** Does the platform flag contradictory or outdated answers, or is that a manual review job?


• **Hallucination control:** Does AI cite sources and admit when it doesn't know, or does it fill gaps with guesses?


• **Narrative-style proposals:** Can it produce prose proposals, not just Q&A grids?


• **Content format flexibility:** How well does it handle Excel, Word, PDF, and PowerPoint imports and exports?


• **Workflow automation:** Can you assign questions, route reviews, and track progress without spreadsheets on the side?


• **Collaboration:** How do occasional reviewers (legal, InfoSec, execs) participate — and are they licensed?


• **Integrations:** Does it connect to your CRM, content stores, and messaging tools? (See the integration table below.)


• **Security and compliance:** SOC 2 status, data handling, and whether your data trains external models.


• **Analytics:** Can you see win rates, cycle times, and content usage?


• **Pricing:** Both vendors quote privately. Model total cost across seats, editions, and add-ons — cross-check vendor quotes against our[RFP software pricing and comparison guide](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfp-software-comparison-guide) .


• **Ease of implementation:** How long to first live RFP, and how much configuration is required?


• **Enterprise scalability:** Does the licensing model hold up as your team and volume grow?

## **Qvidian: Overview, Features, and Limitations**


Qvidian, now part of Upland Software, is an established RFP and proposal automation platform built around a central content library. It's most common in large enterprises — financial services, technology, and healthcare — where consistency across many proposals matters and Microsoft Office is the daily working environment.


### **Qvidian's best features**


• Strong content management and library, cited by users for keeping proposals consistent.


• Deep Microsoft Office integration — pull approved library content directly into Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.


• Reusable content "bundles" that speed up assembling shell documents.


• Document automation for repeatable proposal structures.


• Salesforce and Microsoft 365 connectivity plus an Open API.


• Browser extension (Qvidian for Web) for working across tools.


### **Qvidian's limitations**


• Search and indexing precision is the most-cited weakness — users[want semantic search and more contextual ranking](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews) , and indexing/search is[flagged as the main hitch](https://www3.technologyevaluation.com/solutions/53942/qvidian) by reviewers.


• Third-party summaries[report an outdated UI, slow search, and complex implementation](https://www.sifthub.io/blog/qvidian-pricing-reviews-features-breakdown) (confirm on live listings).


• AI answering is less prominent than in AI-first tools; drafting leans on stored content.


• Pricing is quote-only, which lengthens evaluation. Teams weighing options often review[Qvidian alternatives and how they compare](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/qvidian-competitors-alternatives) before committing.


• Best fit skews to large enterprises; smaller teams may find it heavier than needed.


• Conflict/duplicate detection relies largely on manual library upkeep.


**Qvidian pricing:** No public price is listed by Upland. A third party estimates roughly $15,000–$25,000/year for a base license — an estimate, not vendor-confirmed. Get a written quote for your seat count, and see our[full Qvidian pricing, features, and reviews breakdown](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/qvidian-pricing-features-reviews) for more detail.


**Ratings and reviews:** G2[4.3 (~155–166 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews) , Capterra[4.4 (~42 reviews)](https://www.capterra.com/p/6944/Qvidian-Proposal-Automation/reviews/) , TrustRadius[8.8/10 (37 reviews)](https://www.trustradius.com/products/qvidian-rfp-proposal-automation/reviews) — all reported; confirm on live listings.


***Positive:*** *"I have used Qvidian for almost two years now and couldn't see myself doing my job without it." —*[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/6944/Qvidian-Proposal-Automation/reviews/)


***Mixed:*** *"I think the search functionality in Upland Qvidian could be improved with semantic search and a more contextualized approach to show more accurate responses at the top." —*[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews)


## **Responsive (formerly RFPIO): Overview, Features, and Limitations**


Responsive, formerly RFPIO and headquartered in Beaverton, positions itself as a Strategic Response Management platform. It pairs a large Answer Library with AI-driven answering across RFPs, RFIs,[DDQs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-ddq-software) , and security questionnaires, and is known for project organization and collaboration.


### **Responsive's best features**


• Answer Library plus AI answering, praised for fast, reusable responses.


• Project organization: assign questions, track progress, and reuse prior answers.


• Import/export flexibility across Word, Excel, and PDF.


• Broad integration set including Salesforce, Slack, Teams, SharePoint, and HubSpot.


• Coverage across multiple response types — not just RFPs, but DDQs and security questionnaires.


• Collaboration tooling suited to cross-functional response teams.


### **Responsive's limitations**


• Licensing is[reported as not scaling cost-effectively for larger teams](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/reviews/) .


•[No free reviewer-only access](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) , which can inflate license counts for occasional legal, security, or exec reviewers.


•[Very complex Excel spreadsheets can be difficult to import](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews) due to field setup.


•[AI still needs refinement to avoid altering library responses](https://www.g2.com/compare/loopio-vs-responsive-formerly-rfpio) .


• Pricing is quote-only across all editions; total cost depends heavily on add-ons. Teams often scan[Responsive alternatives and how pricing compares](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfpio-competitors-alternatives) during evaluation.


• Breadth can mean a longer configuration and onboarding runway for smaller teams.


**Responsive pricing:** The[vendor pricing page](https://www.responsive.io/pricing) lists editions (Emerging, Growth, Enterprise) all marked "Contact sales" with no dollar figures.[Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/responsive) describes a per-named-user subscription with edition tiers and optional add-ons (AI content suggestions, advanced integrations), usually quoted annually and often multi-year. A third party estimates core subscriptions from ~$5,000 to $29,000+ depending on team size — an estimate, not vendor-confirmed. For a deeper look, see our[Responsive software pricing and plans comparison](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/responsive-ai-rfpio-pricing-features-reviews) .


**Ratings and reviews:** G2[4.5 (~1,300 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews) , Capterra[4.6 (~249 reviews)](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/reviews/) , TrustRadius[8.9/10 (52 reviews)](https://www.trustradius.com/products/responsive/reviews) — all reported; confirm on live listings.


**Positive:** "Responsive is a total lifesaver for RFPs and security questionnaires!" —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews)


**Mixed:** "The current licensing model doesn't support scaling without breaking the bank." —[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/reviews/)


## **AI Capabilities: How Qvidian and Responsive Compare**


Direct answer: Responsive leads on visible AI answering; Qvidian leans on library retrieval and document assembly, with users still asking for smarter search.


**Qvidian**


• Retrieves and reuses approved library content; strong at consistent document assembly.


• Users request[semantic search and more contextual ranking](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews) — a sign AI relevance can miss.


**Responsive**


• AI answering suggests and imports reusable responses across question types.


• Reviewers note the[AI can still alter library responses](https://www.g2.com/compare/loopio-vs-responsive-formerly-rfpio) and needs refinement.


**Note:** Both platforms grew from content-library foundations, so their AI is layered onto retrieval rather than built to draft and validate autonomously. If autonomous drafting with citations and confidence scores is your priority, see how[AI-native RFP tools approach response quality](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-rfp-software) .

## **Pricing: How Much Does Qvidian Cost vs Responsive?**


Direct answer: Neither vendor publishes prices — both are quote-only, so exact cost depends on seats, editions, and add-ons.


• **Qvidian:** No official price. A third party estimates ~$15,000–$25,000/year for a base license (estimate, not confirmed).


• **Responsive:** Editions all show["Contact sales"](https://www.responsive.io/pricing) ;[Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/responsive) describes per-named-user pricing with add-ons; a third party estimates ~$5,000–$29,000+ (estimate, not confirmed).


**Note:** Reviewer licensing is the hidden cost on both sides. Responsive users flag[no free reviewer-only seats](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) ; confirm Qvidian's seat model too. Occasional legal, InfoSec, and exec reviewers can quietly raise your license count, so model total cost of ownership — not just the sticker figure — before you sign.


## **Reviews: What Users Say About Qvidian and Responsive**


Responsive carries a larger review base and marginally higher scores; Qvidian's smaller base still rates well but flags search and UI. Both are established, credible platforms.


• **Qvidian:** G2 4.3, Capterra 4.4, TrustRadius 8.8/10 — praised for library consistency, criticized for search precision and UI (all reported; confirm live).


• **Responsive:** G2 4.5, Capterra 4.6, TrustRadius 8.9/10 — praised for AI answering and collaboration, criticized for licensing cost at scale (all reported; confirm live).


If you're chasing the "Qvidian vs Responsive Reddit" style of candid feedback, cross-check these listings against practitioner threads before deciding.


## **Security and Compliance**


Both vendors serve regulated enterprises and handle security questionnaires — a use case a wave of[dedicated AI security-questionnaire tools](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-ai-agent-for-security-questionnaires) also target — so verify each platform's current certifications, data-handling terms, and whether your content is used to train external models during your security review. Neither vendor's specific certifications are restated here — request current documentation directly.


**Note:** Data handling is table stakes in this category, but the details differ by vendor and edition. Ask each provider, in writing, how AI features process and store your response content — and whether reviewer access and audit logs meet your compliance team's bar.


## **Is Qvidian Better Than Responsive?**


Direct answer: Neither is universally better — it depends on what your team needs.


Choose **Qvidian** if you want a mature, library-centric proposal engine, live deep inside Microsoft Office, and you're a large enterprise that values document-assembly consistency. Choose **Responsive** if you want broader AI answering across RFPs, DDQs, and security questionnaires, wider integrations, and stronger project collaboration — and you can model the seat-based licensing at your scale.


Weigh the recurring themes: Qvidian's search precision and UI, Responsive's licensing cost at scale. Both grew from content-library roots, so both share the same structural question — how much manual library upkeep and human editing your team is prepared to own.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Is Qvidian better than Responsive?**


Neither is universally better. Qvidian suits large enterprises wanting library-driven proposal automation deep in Microsoft Office; Responsive suits teams wanting broader AI answering and collaboration across RFPs, DDQs, and security questionnaires. Match each to your workflow during demos.


### **How much does Qvidian cost?**


Qvidian doesn't publish pricing — it's quote-only. A third party estimates roughly[$15,000–$25,000/year](https://www.sifthub.io/blog/qvidian-pricing-reviews-features-breakdown) for a base license, but that's an estimate, not a vendor-confirmed figure. Request a written quote for your seat count.


### **How much does Responsive cost?**


Responsive is also quote-only; its[editions](https://www.responsive.io/pricing) all read "Contact sales." Vendr describes per-named-user pricing with add-ons, and a third party estimates[~$5,000–$29,000+](https://www.proposify.com/blog/responsive-io-pricing-guide) depending on team size — again, an estimate, not confirmed.


### **Which has better AI, Qvidian or Responsive?**


Responsive offers more visible AI answering; Qvidian leans on library retrieval and document assembly, with users requesting smarter, more contextual search. Both layer AI onto a content-library foundation, so test draft quality on your own edge-case questions.


### **What is an alternative to Qvidian and Responsive?**


Alternatives include[Loopio](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/loopio-vs-inventive-ai) , Proposify, and a newer category of AI-native, agentic platforms.
